claim: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling calls other AWS services through a service-linked role named AWSServiceRoleForAutoScaling, which it creates the first time you create an Auto Scaling group unless you create and specify a custom suffix role.
question: Which IAM role does EC2 Auto Scaling use to launch and terminate instances for you, and when is it created?

qualifiers.condition: unless a custom suffix service-linked role is specified

evidence.quote: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling uses service-linked roles for the permissions that it requires to call other AWS services on your behalf.

Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling creates the AWSServiceRoleForAutoScaling service-linked role for you the first time that you create an Auto Scaling group, unless you manually create a custom suffix service-linked role and specify it when creating the group.

claim: A service-linked role is a secure way to delegate permissions because only the linked service can assume it, and it makes the API calls the service makes for you visible in AWS CloudTrail.
question: Why is a service-linked role a secure way to let EC2 Auto Scaling act for you?

values.display: only the linked service can assume a service-linked role

evidence.quote: Service-linked roles provide a secure way to delegate permissions to other AWS services because only the linked service can assume a service-linked role.
Service-linked roles also enable all API calls to be visible through AWS CloudTrail.

note: Security lens. Display is 9 words but a verbatim phrase; registrar may cut to 'only the linked service can assume'.

claim: The EC2 Auto Scaling service-linked role can use AWS managed keys but has no access to customer managed KMS keys; to launch instances with EBS volumes encrypted by a customer managed key, you must set up the key policy to allow the role.
question: Why can an Auto Scaling group fail to launch instances whose EBS volumes use a customer managed KMS key, and what fixes it?

values.display: do not include access to your customer managed keys

qualifiers.condition: EBS encryption with a customer managed key

evidence.quote: The predefined permissions also include access to your AWS managed keys.
However, they do not include access to your customer managed keys, allowing you to maintain full control over these keys.
This topic describes how to set up the key policy that you need to launch Auto Scaling instances when you specify a customer managed key for Amazon EBS encryption.

note: Security lens. Classic trap: encrypted launch fails until the key policy allows the service-linked role.

claim: EC2 Auto Scaling needs no additional authorization to use the default AWS managed key for encrypted volumes.
question: Does EC2 Auto Scaling need key policy changes to use the default AWS managed EBS key?

evidence.quote: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling does not need additional authorization to use the default AWS managed key to protect the encrypted volumes in your account.

claim: To give granular access to one specific customer managed key, AWS says to use a custom suffix service-linked role (for example AWSServiceRoleForAutoScaling_suffix) rather than the default role.
question: Which service-linked role should you use to grant granular access to one customer managed key?

qualifiers.condition: granular access to a specific customer managed key

evidence.quote: However, if you plan to give granular access to a specific customer managed key, you should use a custom suffix service-linked role.

claim: A launch configuration cannot specify a customer managed KMS key (KmsKeyId) for EBS encryption; use a launch template to specify it.
question: Can a launch configuration specify a customer managed KMS key for EBS encryption?

values.display: not available when you use a launch configuration

evidence.quote: Note that the `KmsKeyId` option to specify a customer managed key is not available when you use a launch configuration.
To specify your customer managed key, use a launch template instead.

claim: An interface VPC endpoint (AWS PrivateLink) lets you call the EC2 Auto Scaling APIs privately, keeping traffic between the VPC and the service on the AWS network, with no internet gateway, NAT device or virtual private gateway needed.
question: How can instances in a private subnet call the EC2 Auto Scaling API without internet access?

values.display: don't need an internet gateway, a NAT device

evidence.quote: You can improve the security posture of your VPC by configuring Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling to use an interface VPC endpoint.

Interface endpoints are powered by AWS PrivateLink, a technology that enables you to privately access Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling APIs by restricting all network traffic between your VPC and Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling to the AWS network.
With interface endpoints, you also don't need an internet gateway, a NAT device, or a virtual private gateway.

claim: AWS recommends never putting confidential or sensitive information in the user data passed to an instance, or in tags and free-form name fields.

evidence.quote: We also recommend that you never put confidential or sensitive information in the user data that will get passed to an instance.

claim: EC2 instances use basic monitoring by default, with metric data at five-minute intervals; for an additional charge, detailed monitoring gives one-minute data, which AWS recommends for scaling because stale five-minute data slows the response.
question: Why does AWS recommend detailed monitoring for instances that scale, and what does it cost?

evidence.quote: By default, EC2 instances are enabled for basic monitoring, which means metric data for instances is available at five-minute intervals.
For an additional charge, you can enable detailed monitoring to get metric data for instances at a one-minute frequency.
Scaling on metrics with a five-minute frequency can result in a slower response time and scaling on stale metric data.

claim: AWS Auto Scaling has no additional charge; you pay only for the AWS resources your application runs on and for Amazon CloudWatch monitoring fees.
question: What do you pay for when you use AWS Auto Scaling?

values.display: no additional charge for AWS Auto Scaling

evidence.quote: There is no additional charge for AWS Auto Scaling.
You pay only for the AWS resources needed to run your applications and Amazon CloudWatch monitoring fees.
